// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.

}) => any;

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the BBB_Martins training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_bbb = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

PAMPA (parallel artificial membrane permeability assay) is a commonly employed non-cell-based assay to evaluate drug permeability across the cellular membrane.

## functions

namespace functions {

smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the PAMPA_NCATS training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_pampa = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

(A) is not permeable to cell membranes in a PAMPA assay (B) is permeable to cell membranes in a PAMPA assay

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the HIA_Hou training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_hia = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) cannot be absorbed (B) can be absorbed
Drug SMILES: CN(N=O)C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@@H](O)O[C@@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

Please think step by step and use the relevant tools in your analysis. Then put your final choice, (A) or (B), after "Answer:"<|end|><|start|>assistant

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-04-13

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: Mutagenicity means the ability of a drug to induce genetic alterations. Drugs that can cause damage to the DNA can result in cell death or other severe adverse effects. Nowadays, the most widely used assay for testing the mutagenicity of compounds is the Ames experiment which was invented by a professor named Ames. The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the HIA_Hou training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_hia = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the SARSCoV2_Vitro_Touret training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_sarscov2_vitro = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.
Context: SARS-CoV-2 is a coronavirus that causes the COVID-19 disease and has led to millions of deaths worldwide within a few years. Discovering new drugs that can inhibit viral replication would be useful for combatting the virus. One method is to screen a library of small molecule drugs for inhibition in an infected cell-based assay.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) does not inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication (B) inhibits SARS-CoV-2 replication

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.

// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.

// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.

}) => any;

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_cyp2c9 = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the hERG training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_herg = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.

Reasoning: medium

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the ClinTox training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_clintox = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

}) => any;

The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

# Tools

namespace functions {

type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

}) => any;

type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {

feature_names?: string[],

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,

// Find nearest neighbors from the Carcinogens_Lagunin training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_carcinogens = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],

num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the ClinTox training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_clintox = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.

// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.

}) => any;

The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.

(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.
Calls to these tools must go to the commentary channel: 'functions'.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the PAMPA_NCATS training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_pampa = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// List of feature categories to compute.

// Find nearest neighbors from the BBB_Martins training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// List of feature categories to compute.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. # Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the Skin_Reaction training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_skin = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

namespace functions {

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.

// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,

feature_names?: string[],

include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;
